With no direct edge, an extra conv path compensates for the lost route.
Replacing a conv on edge 0 with a skip loses learned features, unlike replacing a weaker op.
Replacing the identity shortcut with a pool removes the best gradient path and blurs the signal.
With a strong conv already on the 0-1-2 route, another conv on 1-3 shows diminishing returns.
Replacing a conv with a pool discards capacity, which is worse than pooling over a weaker op.
Removing a 3x3 conv costs more than removing a pool, skip or none.
Replacing a 3x3 conv on the exit edge with pooling discards learned capacity.
